1.w: [“] I have made A covenant with my eyes; and how could I gaze upon a virgin?

2.w: For what would be the portion of God from above, and the inheritance of Shaddai in the heights?

3.w: Is not disaster for the perverse one and calamity for the workers of iniquity?

4.w: Does He not see my ways, and count all my steps?

5.w: If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried toward deceit,

6.w: let Him weigh me in the scales of justice, and let God know my integrity.

7.w: If my step has turned aside from the way, and my heart has walked, following my eyes, and on my palms has stuck a spot,

8.w: [then] let me sow, and another may eat, and may my crops be uprooted!

9.w: If my heart has been enticed over a woman, or I have lain in wait at the door of my neighbor,

10.w: [then] let my wife grind for another, and others bend down over her.

11.w: For it [is] wickedness, and it [is] to be judged an iniquity.

12.w: For it is a fire [that] devours unto Abaddon, and it would uproot among all my produce.

13.w: If I have rejected the justice of my manservant or my maidservant, in their dispute with me,

14.w: then what shall I do when God arises? And when He inspects, how shall I answer him?

15.w: Did not the One making me in the belly make them, and [that] One prepare us in the womb?

16.w: If I have withheld the poor from pleasure and made to fail the eyes of the widow,

17.w: and have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless could not eat from it—

18.w: indeed from my youth I brought him up as a father, and from the womb of my mother I guided her—

19.w: if I have seen one perishing from lack of clothing, or there [being] no covering for the needy,

20.w: if his loins have not blessed me for warming him by the fleece of my sheep,

21.w: if I have raised my hand against the fatherless, because I saw my help at the gate,

22.w: [then] let my upper arm fall from its shoulder, and my arm be broken [off] from its socket.

23.w: For a calamity from God [is] dread to me, and His majesty I cannot overpower.

24.w: If I have set my confidence [upon] gold, or to fine gold I have said, “My trust;”

25.w: if I have rejoiced because my wealth [was] great, and because my hand had acquired much;

26.w: if I have seen the light when it shines, or the moon moving [in] splendor,

27.w: so that my heart has been enticed in secret, and my hand has kissed my mouth,

28.w: [then] this also be judged an iniquity, for I would have lied to God above.

29.w: If I have rejoiced in the destruction of one hating me, or raised myself up because evil found him—

30.w: though I had not given my mouth to sin by asking with a curse for his life—

31.w: if the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who will give from his flesh not having been satisfied?’—

32.w: A sojourner does not lodge in the street, [for] I have opened my doors to the traveler—

33.w: if I have covered my transgressions like Adam, by hiding my guilt in my bosom,

34.w: because I feared the great multitude, and the contempt of the clans terrified me and I kept silent, not going out the door—

35.w: (Who will give to me one listening to me? Behold, my mark and let Shaddai answer me! And the bill the man of my dispute that has written!

36.w: If not, I would take it up upon my shoulder, [and] bind it as crowns to myself.

37.w: The count of my steps I would declare to him; like a prince I would approach Him.)—

38.w: If my land cries out against me, and together its furrows weep;

39.w: if I have eaten its power without silver, and I have caused to breathe out the soul of its workers,

40.w: [then] in place of the wheat let a thorn come forth, and weeds in place of barley.” The words of Job have ended.
